text:
zoe-sales: Quick heads-up ClientCorp POC: they want Redwood Private in their AWS account (spoke VPC). Constraints: all egress must flow through their TLS-inspect proxy, SOC requires original client IPs in request logs, and they need a tiny stable allowlist to file in this week's firewall change window. Can we propose a low-effort topology and a one-line firewall entry?

matt-net: Two practical options with pros/cons:
1) PrivateLink (AWS interface endpoint) -> Redwood-managed connector. Pro: minimal infra for customer. Con: endpoint ENI IPs are per-AZ and can change (not ideal for strict static allowlist). Also if their proxy SNATs, we only see proxy IPs unless proxy injects X-Forwarded-For.
2) Connector deployed in-customer VPC (recommended for audit): NLB (TCP) in front of connector + 2 EIPs on the NLB for HA. NLB TCP passthrough preserves client IP at the TCP layer so connector can log original source. Customer owns small infra but gets stable EIPs for allowlist.

ana-se: Quick note on TLS/mTLS and ALB vs NLB: ALB terminates TLS and will hide source IP at TCP level (X-Forwarded-For header needed). NLB preserves source IP but you must terminate TLS on the connector for mTLS. If the customer's TLS-inspect proxy re-terminates TLS, ask them to avoid SNAT or to forward X-Forwarded-For.

rachel-ps: Procurement snippet: PrivateLink incurs AWS endpoint hourly + per-GB processing; connector-in-VPC means customer pays EC2/NLB/EIP costs but we typically offer a POC infra credit. I'll attach a short estimate to the quote.

deploy-bot: Provisioned ephemeral POC connector stack in acct 555666777888 (us-east-1). id: pc-connector-555. NLB created, awaiting EIP allocation.

matt-net: Pasteable firewall ticket (choose variant):
```
# Variant A - Connector-in-VPC (preferred for stable IPs)
Allow TCP/443 from App Subnet 10.40.0.0/22 to Connector NLB EIPs 198.51.100.77 and 198.51.100.78 (outbound)
Allow TCP/443 from Connector NLB EIPs to App LB SG for callback flows (inbound)

# Variant B - PrivateLink (if customer cannot host infra)
Allow TCP/443 from App Subnet 10.40.0.0/22 to Interface Endpoint ENI IPs (ENI IPs provided after endpoint creation). Note: ENI IPs may change if the endpoint is re-created.
```
Also add: "If your proxy performs TLS inspect and SNATs traffic, please configure it to inject X-Forwarded-For and avoid SNAT for these flows to preserve client IPs."

zoe-sales: Good stuff. Owners: matt-net -> final 1-page network runbook + firewall ticket (EOD tomorrow). rachel-ps -> POC cost blurb. ana-se -> security Q answers for mTLS/KMS/log-forwarding. I'll schedule a 30m handoff in the change window. Thanks!
